notes: **Item D1b** = changes 1 and 2 of D1 (Discussion §2 ¶2), shown **together**, because both change the same paragraph. In D1 the preview showed change 2 with the *old* opening ("these resolved at three different levels. On chromosome 7H…"). Without its opening, deleting the 1H sentence looked like a loss.

With both changes, the opening names all three regions: "…which resolved to a single gene on chromosome 7H, to two genes on 3H and to no gene with a known role in either trait on 1H". A separate 1H sentence would then repeat that clause word for word. So it is either option A (both changes) or option B (neither).
questions: **§2 ¶2:** **A** (default): both changes, as shown below; the three regions are named in the opening and 1H is not repeated. **B**: keep the paragraph exactly as it is now (old opening "these resolved at three different levels", plus the separate 1H and 3H sentences).

edits.why: The three regions named in the opening; 1H not repeated; 3H sentence shortened; 7H sentences unchanged.
edits.old: The trade-off also had a genomic counterpart. Fiber and starch loci co-localized in three regions, and these resolved at three different levels. On chromosome 7H, the two loci resolved to a single gene, and a single haplotype of this gene carried both effects, higher fiber and lower starch of similar magnitude. With the two lead SNPs only 154 bp apart and no other annotated gene within 112 kb, this pattern is more simply explained by one causal variant expressed through two correlated traits than by two linked genes. Moreover, the carriers of the minor alleles at this locus, and of the haplotype carrying both effects, came from sites across the environmental gradient of the collection, so this shared signal cannot be explained as a geographic artifact of the accessions' origin. <!-- src (item 11, 2026-09-30): 11_USED_check_low_maf_geographic_distribution_minor_allele/results/tables/T02_lead_enrichment_tests.tsv rows fiber_L17 (41 carriers, 11 sites; N/C/D/HZ1/HZ2/HZ3 = 0/5/7/7/21/1; 17.1% desert vs 15.0% of major carriers; q Desert 0.81) and starch_L05 (35 carriers, 10 sites; 0/5/7/7/14/2; 20.0% vs 18.2%; q 0.82); T04_haplotype_group_enrichment_tests.tsv GDSL haplotype B (34; 0/5/7/7/14/1; 20.6% desert vs 15.1%; q 0.67). Panel desert share 50/290 = 17%. Wording by the user, 2026-09-30 ("all environments", then "sites across the environmental gradient of the collection"): the carriers come from the coast, the desert and the three transitional zones; none from the four northern sites. TODO 403 and comment 412 removed on this item (user). --> The gene encodes a GDSL esterase/lipase rather than a starch enzyme, so its link to starch is more likely compositional than mechanistic, as a shift in the cell-wall fraction changes the share of starch in the grain in the opposite direction. On chromosome 3H, the two neighboring loci resolved to two genes, one per trait, a cutin-biosynthetic acyltransferase (*GPAT6*) for fiber and a plastid phosphate transporter (*PHT4;3*) for starch. On chromosome 1H, the region contained no gene with a known role in either trait. Thus, the carbon-allocation axis was visible at every level the data could resolve.
